I have Tachycardia and issues with heart palpitations. These issues cause me to get dizzy, have shortness of breath, fall and on a few occasions I've passed out.

It isn't easy for me to live a normal life without help, so I have a service dog, Mishka.

For awhile I was too sick to leave the house much. Mishka wasn't working a lot and she needs to brush up on her training. I've been working on doing so for the last few weeks.

Today I went down to the pool in my apartment complex. It was still early and nobody was there. I decided to go get Mishka and work on her pool-side etiquette.

I was in the deep end and I had her in a down-stay, chilling out under a picnic table so she could be in the shade.

She whined at me. Not how she usually alerts me, but it got my attention. My heart started fluttering. She ran up to the side of the pool and started barking her head off, like I've never heard her do before. She usually nudges me or does a combination of a bark and nudging.

I was able to get to the edge of the pool right before things started going black. I managed to hold onto the ledge until it passed.

If I hadn't gone and got her, I would have drowned. I was still the only person there when it happened.

Even though she still occasionally gets distracted, I don't think I'll be leaving without her anytime soon...I'll just train her on the go...
My dog saved my life today.
I'm glad Mishka saved the day! I never knew service dogs could help with heart issues in this way. That's really good to know!
dogs are wonderful at detecting health issues like this... they have seizure dogs also.
